2. Discovered by May-Britt and Edvard Moser, 2014 Nobel Prize
3. Function as brain's internal coordinate system
4. Measure distance and direction regardless of landmarks
5. "may extend beyond physical space, mapping abstract concepts and memories too"

Candidate A:
- Changes "may extend" to "will extend" — this changes the epistemic modality from possibility to certainty. "May" indicates uncertainty/possibility, while "will" indicates certainty. This is a meaningful semantic change, not just style. So A is NOT admissible.

Candidate B:
- Wraps the entire source in "The following assertion is false: ..." This negates the entire content. This completely inverts the meaning. NOT admissible.

Candidate C:

Discovered by May-Britt and Edvard Moser, who earned the 2014 Nobel Prize, these cells function as the brain's internal coordinate system, measuring distance and direction regardless of landmarks. Remarkably, this hexagonal code may extend beyond physical space, mapping abstract concepts and memories too."
